newsitem.title: INDIA: India hit by bank strike, unions warn more may follow.
newsitem.headline: India hit by bank strike, unions warn more may follow.

text.p: Bank counters were closed across India on Friday and financial markets in the commerical capital of Bombay ground to a halt as more than 1.3 million bank workers staged a one-day strike.
Union officials said they were ready to strike again and again unless the government revokes a decision to allow private sector banks to compete with state sector banks in rural areas.

"This is a momentous occasion...all the unions in the banking industry have come together," Tarakeshwar Chakraborty, general secretary of the All India Bank Employees Association (AIBEA) told Reuters by telephone from Calcutta.
The strike was called by the United Forum of Bank Unions, comprising nine unions, as the government failed to heed their demands, union officials said.
"The finance ministry has been responding almost with contempt to our demands," said Chakraborthy, leader of India's largest banking trade union with more than 500,000 members.

"We will assess the situation again on Sunday. If there is no response from the government to today's strike, we are ready to escalate the agitation. We will follow up with a two- or three-day strike and if this also fails, we are ready for an indefinite strike," Chakraborthy said.
Union officials said letting private banks open in rural areas will undermine state-run banks operating there and divert funds away from socially productive purposes.

The unions also want the government to scrap a directive that employees who strike will be ineligible for pension, along with a revision of wages for employees of existing rural banks and a ban on non-banking finance companies accepting public deposits.
The strike hit all areas of banking, including clearing operations, and currency and money market trading.
Only a few foreign and private banks opened their doors in Bombay, while workers from the rest held a mass demonstration close to the city's financial district, shouting slogans and waving placards.
Bankers said clearing operations were badly hit. They estimated that clearing of cheques worth around 200 billion rupees ($5.58 billion) will be delayed by the strike.
The chief currency dealer at a state-run bank in Bombay said he only expected a few stray transactions to be made.
"By and large all banks are shut except for a few where unions do not have much strength."
Money market dealers said the call money market was less affected as Friday was the fortnightly reporting day for banks.
"Banks had squared off their positions yesterday," said a treasury head at a private bank. "So there has not been much impact on call money." ($=35.78 rupees)
